verdict.evidence:
A: The dialog is red text on black: 'Delete this file?', the full path 'fixtures/ssd-story/Caches/Browser/Media Cache/video-buffer.bin', and a bare '(y/n)'. It does not give the size, say whether deletion is permanent, or say whether a trash exists. The main pane behind the dialog is a blank grey rectangle with no file block or label, so the target cannot be checked visually. The header reads 'Total: 4.2G (39 files), freed: 0'. The keybar lists '<BACKSPACE> - delete', and one 'y' keystroke is all that separates the user from deletion. A corner legend, '(x = Small files)', is unexplained.

B: The dialog is titled 'Permanently delete this item?'. It names 'video-buffer.bin' in bold and states '610.0 MiB on disk · 1 files' inside the dialog. It warns 'This cannot be undone. No trash or recovery.' It requires 'Type delete to confirm:' and labels both exits, 'Esc cancel' and 'Enter delete'. Behind it, the space map block labelled 'video-buffer.bin 610.0 MiB · 100.0%' stays visible. A 'LARGEST FIRST' list shows the same entry, the breadcrumb reads 'ssd-story / Caches / Browser / Media Cache', and '610.0 MiB physical space used' sits at top right. The path in the dialog is truncated to 'ssd-story/Caches/Browser/Media Ca…', so the full location can only be confirmed from the breadcrumb. 'Esc cancel' and 'Enter delete' share the same salmon colour, so the destructive choice is not visually set apart from the safe one. There is no running 'freed' total.
verdict.loser_reason: A lost mainly because its confirmation dialog says nothing about consequences. It gives no size, no statement that deletion is permanent, and no word on whether a trash exists. It sits over an empty grey pane and needs only a single 'y' keypress. The user therefore cannot verify, from the prompt itself, how much space is recovered or what is lost.
